title: Google Search AI Mode rolls out temporary thread feature globally, offering an incognito privacy search experience

content_html:
On November 18, Google announced the official launch of the "Temporary Threads" feature in AI Mode in Search on desktop and mobile browsers worldwide, allowing users to conduct private, non-personalized instant searches so that their query history is not retained in their personal history and does not interfere with subsequent algorithmic recommendations.

This feature draws on the temporary chat mechanism of the standalone app Gemini. Users do not need to change their account privacy settings; they only need to click the temporary conversation icon in the upper-right corner of AI Mode to start a session, and the content is cleared from the interface after it is closed.

As Google introduced the "Personal Intelligence" feature in AI Mode in early 2026, which can draw on context from Gmail and Google Photos, the need for data isolation brought by deep personalization has become increasingly prominent. By cutting the link between sessions and user preference profiles, Temporary Threads effectively solve the problem of one-off searches—such as medical consultations or gift shopping—polluting recommendation models.

However, "front-end invisibility" in technical implementation does not mean immediate destruction on the back end. According to Google's latest privacy policy, temporary conversations and sessions with history turned off will still be retained on servers in association with the user's account for about two months (a significant extension from the previous 72 hours) to generate responses and ensure security, but they are strictly excluded from AI model training.

In addition, anonymized conversations that undergo manual safety review may be retained for up to three years, while enterprise and education accounts follow separate management rules. This move marks that leading tech companies, while advancing deep AI context integration, are improving compliance boundaries and user trust through refined, tiered privacy controls.
